newsitem.title: USA: Florida Power in Crystal River cost pact.
newsitem.headline: Florida Power in Crystal River cost pact.

text.p: Florida Power Corp said Thursday it reached an agreement allowing recovery of $33.8 million, plus interest, of the estimated $170 million in replacement fuel costs expected to be incurred during the extended outage of its Crystal River nuclear unit.
The company said agreement resolves all disputed issues in a case involving its request to collect replacement fuel and purchased power costs associated with the outage that began in September 1996.

The Florida Progress Corp subsidiary reached agreement with the Attorney General of the State of Florida, the Office of Public Counsel, the Florida Industrial Power Users Group, the Florida Consumers Action Network, State Senator Charlie Crist, the Lake Dora Harbour Homeowners Association Inc and the American Association of Retired Persons.
The Florida Public Service Commission is expected to vote on the proposed settlement at the earliest possible date.
If it approves, Florida Power said, it will stop recovery of the portion of its fuel charge associated with the outage.
The utility will immediately refund, with interest, money collected since the increase went into effect on April 1.
The company noted it had been given permission to collect about $2.22 per 1,000 kilowatt-hours on an interim basis. The refund will be a one-time credit on electric bills.
In addition to the refund, the company said, it will maintain its current base rates for the next four years.

And as previously announced by Florida Power, its customers will not bear additional costs related to the capital and non-fuel operating and maintenance expenses associated with the nuclear plant outage.

It said the capital costs of the outage are estimated to be between $30 million and $45 million. The operating and maintenance expenses are estimated at $80 million to $100 million. The total cost of the outage, including replacement fuel, is expected to be between $280 million and $315 million.
The recovery of $33.8 million represents replacement fuel costs from September, October and November of 1996.

The company said it will begin this recovery after the plant returns to service, which is expected to be by year end. To minimize the impact on customers, the cost will be spread over 12 months as part of the fuel charge on electric bills.
Florida Power said the remaining unrecovered replacement fuel costs will be deferred and amortized for up to 48 months and will not result in an increase in customer bills.
To offset a portion of the amortization, Florida Power will temporarily suspend accruing its reserve for fossil plant dismantlement costs for a period of four years.

Prior to the end of the amortization period, the company will submit a study for use by the commission in establishing a revised accrual to the dismantlement reserve. Any increase due to a deficiency in the reserve will be absorbed by Florida Power, the utility said in a statement.
